title: Enterprise LLM Load Testing, Streaming SSE Benchmarking (NVIDIA GenAI-Perf / GuideLLM / Locust) & KV-Cache Saturation Knee Selection

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Legacy HTTP Load Tester (`JMeter / wrk / ab`) with Identical 50-Token Prompt & Non-Streaming `stream=false`
tiers.architecture: Sending 10,000 identical short prompts (`Tell me a joke`) with `stream=false` and measuring only total HTTP response time

tiers.tier: Tier 2: Synthetic Random-Token Streaming Benchmark (`100% Cache-Miss` Uniform Length `4,096 In / 512 Out`)
tiers.architecture: Generating random vocabulary IDs (0% prefix cache hit) at a fixed length without modeling log-normal prompt variance or multi-turn prefix sharing

tiers.tier: Tier 3: Open-Loop Average-Latency Benchmark (Ignoring `Goodput SLO: P99 TTFT <= 800ms & P95 TPOT <= 25ms`)
tiers.architecture: Reporting peak tokens/sec throughput at 256 concurrent requests while ignoring that P99 TTFT has already degraded to 6,200ms

tiers.tier: Tier 4: `NVIDIA GenAI-Perf / GuideLLM + Locust SSE` with Production Log-Normal Token Distribution, Realistic Prefix-Cache Tree & `Goodput SLO` Knee Finder
tiers.architecture: Replaying anonymized production `(ISL, OSL, Prefix_Hit_Ratio)` distributions over SSE streams, sweeping concurrency to pinpoint the `85% KV-Cache Preemption Knee` and sizing by `SLO Goodput`

scenarios.scenario: Why Testing an LLM with `JMeter` and a Single Repeated Prompt Overestimates Capacity by 310%
scenarios.question: A QA team ran JMeter with 200 threads sending the same 100-token prompt (`stream=false`) and reported 'Our 8x H100 cluster easily handles 200 QPS!'; on launch day, the cluster collapsed at 48 QPS
scenarios.model_answer: Sending the **exact same prompt 10,000 times** hits **100% Automatic Prefix Cache** (`0` prefill compute!) and uses tiny KV memory, inflating capacity by **310%** (`Tier 1`)! Conversely, sending **100% random tokens (`Tier 2`)** forces **0% prefix cache hit**, underestimating capacity by 68%! Always benchmark with **`NVIDIA GenAI-Perf / GuideLLM`** configured to replay your **exact production Prefix-Sharing Tree (`e.g., 60% shared system prompt + 40% unique RAG context`) and Log-Normal `(ISL, OSL)` distribution (`3.2%` sizing error)**!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 unintentionally benchmarks 100% prefix-cache hits on short prompts; Tier 2 benchmarks 0% cache hits on random noise.

scenarios.scenario: Measuring Streaming SSE Metrics (`TTFT`, `TPOT`, `ITL`) Instead of Total HTTP Request Duration
scenarios.question: In traditional web load testing (`wrk / JMeter`), a 6-second response is a timeout failure; in LLM streaming, a 200-token answer at 40 tok/s naturally takes 5.3 seconds—how should QA define pass/fail?
scenarios.model_answer: Total HTTP duration (`E2E Latency`) is meaningless without separating **Prefill** from **Decode**! Configure **`GenAI-Perf` or custom `Locust SSE` parsers** to timestamp every Server-Sent Event (`data: chunk`) and gate acceptance on **Three Independent Streaming Metrics**: (1) **`P99 TTFT (Time-To-First-Token) <= 800ms`**, (2) **`P95 TPOT (Time-Per-Output-Token) <= 25ms` (`>= 40 tok/s`)**, and (3) **`P99 ITL (Inter-Token Latency Hitch) <= 80ms`** (to catch chunked-prefill stalls)!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 `stream=false` buffers the entire response, hiding whether a 5s delay was a 4.8s prefill stall or a long 400-token generation.

scenarios.scenario: Finding the 'KV-Cache Saturation & Preemption Knee' (`Goodput` vs. Raw Throughput)
scenarios.question: As we increase concurrent users from 80 to 160 in vLLM, raw token throughput keeps inching up slightly, but P99 TTFT suddenly jumps from 450ms to 5,800ms at 115 users—where is our true capacity limit?
scenarios.model_answer: Never size an LLM cluster by **Peak Raw Tokens/Sec (`Tier 3`)**! At `115` concurrent users, `vLLM`'s `gpu_cache_usage_perc` crosses **`92%–100%`** and triggers **KV-Cache Recomputation/Swap Preemptions**! Size strictly by **`SLO Goodput` (the maximum QPS where `>= 99%` of requests simultaneously satisfy both `TTFT <= 800ms` and `TPOT <= 25ms`)**—which occurs just before the **`85% KV-Cache Utilization Knee`** (`99.2%` goodput)!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 3 reports the concurrency point of maximum raw tok/s, which sits deep inside the KV-cache preemption cliff (`59%` goodput).

scenarios.scenario: End-to-End Pipeline Load Testing (`AI Gateway + Guardrails + Vector DB + TEI Reranker + LLM`)
scenarios.question: Benchmarking `vLLM` in isolation showed 420ms P99 TTFT, but in production the AI Gateway's Redis rate-limiter and Vector Reranker became the bottleneck at 180 QPS
scenarios.model_answer: Run **Two-Layer Acceptance Benchmarks**: (1) **Component Benchmark (`GenAI-Perf -> vLLM/TRT-LLM`)** to tune tensor parallelism and `max_num_batched_tokens`, followed by (2) **Full-Stack Locust SSE Replay (`Gateway -> Guardrail -> Vector/TEI -> LLM`)** under Poisson arrival rates (`0.0%` post-launch SLA breach)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Testing only the bare model container misses connection-pool exhaustion and reranker queueing in the gateway.

perturbation_checks.check: Poisson Burst Arrival Pattern (Peak-to-Average Ratio 2.8x Within 10-Second Windows) vs. Uniform Pacing
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 3.8% Error (Poisson Arrival Replay Reveals Need for 15% KV Headroom Buffer at 85% Watermark)

perturbation_checks.check: 5% Long-Tail 'Monster Prompts' (64K Context Inputs Mixed into a 4K-Mean Workload)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 98.6% Goodput (Log-Normal Replay Verifies Chunked Prefill `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` Protects Decode ITL)

key_findings: Tier 4 (NVIDIA GenAI-Perf / GuideLLM + Locust SSE with Log-Normal Token Distributions, Realistic 60% Prefix-Sharing Trees, and SLO Goodput Knee Detection) reduces capacity sizing error from 310% (Tier 1 JMeter) down to 3.2% and achieves 99.2% production SLO goodput.

Load testing with a single repeated prompt (Tier 1) triggers 100% prefix-cache hits and overestimates production GPU capacity by 3.1x; testing with 100% random tokens (Tier 2) forces 0% cache hits and underestimates capacity by 68%.
Sizing clusters by 'SLO Goodput' (requests meeting both P99 TTFT <= 800ms and P95 TPOT <= 25ms) rather than raw peak tokens/sec prevents operating past the 85% KV-cache preemption cliff.
